transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-27 14:30 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Redwood Partner Ops); Priya Singh, Ethan Park, Liam O'Connor, Zara Malik (Aurora)

Optional summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Redwood intro and partner program overview; Aurora gave background on hardware + go-to-market; discussed integration touchpoints (bring-your-own model images, referral margin, co-marketing). Technical topics: private deployments, Dedicated vs Hosted routing, KV caching, quantization recommendations, SOC2/SAML/KMS. Agreed next steps: share deck, schedule infra deep dive, exchange security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick round robin, I'll kick off, I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Carlos is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Priya (Aurora): Hi, Priya here, Head of Partnerships at Aurora. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:13] Ethan (Aurora): Ethan — solutions lead. Liam (CTO) and Zara (cloud arch) are on as well.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): Great to meet you all. High level we'll do 15 minutes of program + go-to-market, then 20 minutes technical, then quick next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Liam (Aurora): Yep, works.
[00:32] Maya: Cool. I'll start with a very short Redwood primer — sorry if folks have seen this — we're a developer-first inference platform, we run hosted APIs, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deploys. Focus on production economics: latency, cost, and reliability.
[00:50] Zara: Quick question — when you say "private deploys" do you mean full on-prem with no egress to your control plane, or VPC peering? We've got customers that require air gap.
[00:59] Maya: Good question. We offer both flavors. For most partners we do a private control plane with VPC peering and customer-managed networking; we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped/regulated customers. There are some extra professional services for air-gap installs.
[01:15] Priya: Nice. That matches a lot of asks we hear. Aurora does hardware and also runs managed clusters for enterprise customers; a lot of them ask for both dedicated hosting and private egress.
[01:28] Carlos: From a technical lens, a few quick clarifiers — what models & frameworks do your customers typically run? TensorFlow/PyTorch? Are they using Hugging Face or custom model images?
[01:38] Ethan: Mostly PyTorch and HF models, but some customers bring custom container images for optimized runtimes. We have a mix — A100 fleets today, some customers testing H100. Also a few inference-optimized amps with 80GB.
[01:55] Carlos: Got it. When you say "bring custom images" do you have a standard OCI registry setup, or is it split per customer?
[02:02] Zara: We host a private registry per tenant, but for partners we can do a shared partner registry with signed images.
[02:08] Maya: That helps a lot. Two things from Redwood side that usually come up in integrations: 1) model packaging + kernel selection — we can accept docker images or work with model artifacts, and 2) routing policies for dedicated vs hosted — partners often want to route burst traffic to hosted then fall back to dedicated.
[02:26] Liam: Is that routing policy configurable per-customer? Like can we set latency SLOs and fallback thresholds?
[02:32] Carlos: Yes, per-route policies. You can set latency targets, cost thresholds, region affinity; if dedicated capacity is saturated there's automated fallback to compatible model variants in hosted or a lower precision quantized variant.
[02:44] Liam: Speaking of quantization, what's your support for lower precision — int8, nf4, etc. And do you do that automatically?
[02:50] Carlos: We support FP16, int8, and nf4 profiles. We give recommendations based on workload footprints and quality monitoring — Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles and we can run small sample evals. It's not always fully automatic — we surface tradeoffs and can run canary rollouts.
[03:04] Ethan: And latency numbers — roughly what do we see on A100 vs H100? Customers will ask about per-token latency.
[03:10] Maya: It depends a lot on sequence lengths and batching. For 2048-ish context on A100 we see X tokens/ms ranges — sorry I'm being vague — Carlos, want to add numbers?
[03:20] Carlos: Sure, rough rule of thumb: on well-optimized kernels H100 can be 20-40% faster for common transformer models versus A100 for long context; but again depends on quantization and kernels. Also, our continuous batching can change tail latency numbers; we tune batching policies by customer SLO.
[03:38] Priya: From partner perspective, our sales team wants crisp cost comps so we can position Aurora + Redwood as an integrated offering. Do you have a partner pricing model or referral margin?
[03:50] Janelle (Redwood Partner Ops): We have partner tiers — referral and reseller paths. We can share the partner program deck after this call. Margins are standard, and we also do co-sell credits for first pilots.
[03:59] Priya: Great. We'll want the deck and a sample contract language.
[04:03] Maya: Absolutely. We'll share partner deck and a sample MSA addendum.
[04:08] Zara: On security — SOC 2, KMS, SSO, audit logs — can you summarize?
[04:14] Carlos: We are SOC 2 Type II, standard SAML/SSO and RBAC. For private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management; logs are plumbed into your SIEM via syslog or S3 delivery. We also have audit trails per-token for requests when required for compliance.
[04:30] Liam: Is there an easy path for customers to use their own KMS so plaintext never leaves their boundary?
[04:35] Carlos: Yes on private deploys — the control plane can be configured so keys never transit our systems; for hosted API it's envelope encryption with customer-managed keys and tight retention controls.
[04:45] Ethan: Can you share the security whitepaper or questionnaire? Our security folks will want to run a full vendor assessment.
[04:50] Maya: We'll attach that doc in the follow-up.
[04:54] Priya: On the technical integration, a couple asks — one: how do you handle KV cache across sharded models? Two: can we surface per-tenant caching metrics?
[05:03] Carlos: Good Q. We manage KV cache in the serving layer; when models are sharded across GPUs we maintain per-session KV shards and stitch on the fly. You can export cache hit/miss metrics per-tenant and we expose those via the console and tracing hooks. (note: auto transcript sometimes shows KV as "K-V cash")
[05:22] Zara: Nice, that visibility is helpful. For our managed customers we like to see cache hit percentages per route.
[05:28] Carlos: Totally, we can add those dashboards to the partner view.
[05:32] Priya: Another product question — how do you recommend we sell dedicated vs hosted? Most of our customers start with hosted but then move to dedicated when SLOs are strict.
[05:43] Maya: That's common. Hosted gives fast onboarding and you can do trials quickly; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation for enterprise. For partners, we often position a joint offering: pilot on hosted, baseline on dedicated, and private for regulated customers.
[05:56] Liam: For pilots, how long does provisioning for Dedicated usually take?
[05:59] Carlos: Depends on capacity availability — with reserved capacity it's days to a couple weeks if GPU inventory is available; for bare-metal/private installs it's longer — typically 4-8 weeks including networking and security reviews.
[06:10] Ethan: For the benchmark tests, can Redwood run a performance test on our hardware, or do we need to host models in Redwood's infra?
[06:18] Carlos: We can do both. We have a partner benchmark harness that can run on your clusters (we provide a runner) or we can run the same tests in our Dedicated environment. Running locally helps find kernel mismatches and profiling issues early.
[06:31] Priya: That sounds perfect. We'll want a list of the runner requirements.
[06:35] Carlos: We'll include that in the follow-up.
[06:38] Maya: Quick commercial question — do you have a preferred contract flow? Do Aurora customers buy through you and then we invoice, or are you reselling and want consolidated billing?
[06:48] Priya: We prefer reseller arrangements for managed customers, but some enterprise accounts want direct vendor contracts. Flexible depending on the customer.
[06:56] Maya: Okay we'll note that.
[07:00] Liam: One more deep tech thing — model parallelism: are there models that you won't support in certain deployment modes? For example, very large model sharded across custom NVLink topologies?
[07:12] Carlos: Some extreme sharding setups need careful co-design. We support standard model parallelism patterns (tensor/model parallelism) but if it's a highly custom NVLink fabric we might need engineering time to validate. That's where the deep-dive and a bench-on-your-farm test helps.
[07:27] Zara: Understood. We have a handful of customers running 64+ GPU clusters with custom fabrics.
[07:33] Maya: Ok sounds like a good candidate for engineering validation. We'll set that as a follow-up.
[07:37] Ethan: Operational question: do you provide autoscaling for Dedicated pools? We want to offer burst capacity for peak times.
[07:45] Carlos: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options — you can define min/max pool sizes and burst rules. During spikes requests can route to hosted for overflow if you enable that.
[07:58] Priya: Any limitations on the models used for burst routing? I.e. do you only allow serving of identical model variants in hosted fallback?
[08:06] Carlos: Fallback is to compatible model variants. Typically you'd have a quantized or distilled variant in hosted as fallback; we also support model aliasing so the service name remains consistent even if the backend variant changes.
[08:18] Liam: About observability — do you expose token-level costs and latency per-request?
[08:24] Carlos: Yes, our console has token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. You can hook up your tracing provider. For partner dashboards we can show aggregated metrics per-tenant.
[08:36] Priya: Are there rate-limits or quotas that partners need to be aware of for pilots?
[08:41] Maya: For pilots we usually bump quotas; we have standard rate-limits but partner pilots can get temporary lifts. We'll coordinate on expected volumes.
[08:49] Ethan: On compliance, any customers requiring data residency controls? We have EU customers who require EU-only processing.
[08:55] Maya: We support region affinity and can pin workloads to regions. For hosted we have region-based control planes; for private installs obviously you control residency.
[09:05] Liam: What's the typical SLO for latency you guarantee on Dedicated?
[09:09] Carlos: It depends on the commit tier; for enterprise reserved capacity we can contract SLOs — 99.9p tail latency targets at a route level are common in SLAs, but exact numbers depend on commit and model shape.
[09:22] Priya: Do you have references of customers in regulated industries?
[09:26] Maya: Yes, we have healthcare and fintech customers on private deployments; happy to provide reference list under NDA.
[09:33] Zara: For the technical deep-dive, can we get a list of artifacts Redwood needs? e.g., model artifacts, perf traces, environment specs?
[09:41] Carlos: We'll request hardware inventory, container images OR model artifacts, network topology, GPU firmware/driver versions, and a sample workload with expected QPS and typical prompt distributions.
[09:54] Priya: We'll compile that and try to have it ready ahead of the deep dive.
[09:59] Maya: Great. A couple of misc notes — we sometimes run joint benchmarking blog posts and co-marketing when partners want. Priya, is that interesting for Aurora?
[10:08] Priya: Yes, co-marketing is high on our list. We can coordinate on a joint benchmark piece.
[10:12] Maya: Perfect.
[10:15] (short pause)
[10:20] Liam: One thought — for billing, are there minimums for Dedicated?
[10:24] Janelle: There are reserved capacity packages with monthly commits; we have flexible tiers for partners. We'll send the partner pricing grid.
[10:31] Ethan: Any documentation available for the partner API or provisioning flows?
[10:35] Maya: Yes we'll share a partner portal link and the onboarding playbook.
[10:39] Priya: Ok, for next steps can we call out owners?
[10:42] Maya: Sure — I'll recap.
[10:44] Maya: Action items recap: Maya to send partner deck, pricing tiers, sample MSA addendum. Carlos to schedule infra deep dive and send runner requirements. Priya to share hardware inventory and typical workloads. Janelle to coordinate partner account creation and CRM sync. We'll also exchange security docs.
[11:04] Liam: Sounds good.
[11:06] Zara: One small nit from our eng team — how do you handle GPU driver mismatches during deployments? We prefer not to have to patch drivers across customer fleets.
[11:15] Carlos: We version our runtime and document supported driver versions; for partner-run clusters we can provide containerized runtimes that reduce dependency on host driver versions, but for best perf sometimes driver updates are required. We'll surface that during benching.
[11:27] Priya: Anything else?
[11:29] Maya: No that's it from our side. Thanks everyone for a productive call. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[11:37] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward to it.
[11:40] (meeting ends)
